Generate lorem ipsum placeholder text for layouts, mockups and designs — by paragraph, by sentence or by exact word count. The text is the classic passage from the printing trade: pseudo-Latin derived from Cicero's De Finibus Bonorum et Malorum, scrambled in the 1500s so that it looks like real copy without meaning anything. Designers use it because a reader's eye slides over it instead of reading it, so the layout — not the words — gets judged.

## How to use the Lorem Ipsum Generator

Start by entering your how many, then choosing your generate from the list. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Choose paragraphs, sentences or words.
2. Enter how many you need.
3. Copy the generated text into your design.

## Formula

Paragraphs are built from the classic lorem ipsum sentences in rotation, 3–5 sentences each; sentences mode takes them in order; words mode takes the first N words of the passage.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Lorem Ipsum Generator](/lorem-ipsum-generator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Where lorem ipsum comes from

The text is a mangled version of Cicero's De Finibus Bonorum et Malorum (45 BC), beginning 'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit' — roughly 'there is no one who loves pain itself'. A 16th-century printer scrambled the words so the text would fill a type specimen without distracting readers, and it has been the standard placeholder ever since. It is public-domain text, free to use anywhere.

## Why designers use nonsense text

Real words pull the eye: a reviewer reads the copy instead of judging the layout, the spacing and the type. Lorem ipsum has the rhythm and word lengths of English without the meaning, so it shows how a page will look without inviting anyone to proofread it. The rule of thumb: use placeholder text while the design is being judged, and swap in real copy before the design is signed off — a layout that only works with lorem ipsum is not finished.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Use paragraphs for page mockups, sentences for short blocks, and words when a space is exactly sized.
- The first sentence is always the famous opening — everyone recognises it as placeholder text.
- Replace placeholder text with real copy before sign-off: a design that depends on it is not finished.
